newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares listless on low trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares listless on low trade.

text.p: Russian shares opened little changed on Thursday, with most leading shares little changed from Wednesday's close, and traders said they did not expect any sharp moves over the rest of the day.
"Today's situation is just in line with the trend typical of the first half of the current week -- the lack of large orders and low trading volumes," said Nikolai Grikhachev of Rossiisky Kredit Bank.
"Even the LUKoil news did not influence the market trend," he said.
LUKoil said it had signed a $5 billion joint venture with Atlantic Richfield Co to develop oil and gas projects in Russia and abroad.
At 0920 GMT LUKoil was at $9.58, up from Wednesday's closing $9.56, but off an early $9.62 high.
Alexander Gritskevich of Trinfiko said he expected the market to remain listless on Friday and probably next week.
"Maybe the market has taken a wait-and-see attitude towards President Boris Yeltsin's future heart operation," he said.
"Trading volumes are just small, and profits are in part eaten away by the re-registration of shares."
UES eased to $0.0778 from $0.0780. Norilsk Nickel fell to $6.62 from $6.70, and traders said this was due to the plant's current financial problems.
Retailer GUM edged down to $19.30 from $19.50 on profit-taking after recent steady buying.
